card.title: Decompose
card.subtitle: break the passage into moves
card.status_plain: The moves for this passage exist (60 of them, with 49 connections). They were read from a retyped copy, not yet the checkout, so this is a worked example, honest about that.

what_it_is: Decompose breaks the checked-out passage into moves. A move is one action the text makes: an agent does an operation to something, with a result. It turns a block of text into an ordered list of small, labeled actions the rest of the method reads.
why_it_matters: The move is the unit the whole method works on, and it is where making the unsaid said begins. A gap is what a move leaves unsaid, so you cannot name a silence until you have named the moves it sits between. Every later step reads moves: the gaps hang off them, the later readings answer each move's question, the comparisons line moves up across texts. So the move boundary is load-bearing. Break the passage well and the reading holds. Break it badly and every step downstream inherits the error.

how_it_works.you give it: two things: the checked-out passage (the exact sourced text the Text step handed over), and the one question you are reading it for (this decides what counts as important). The year and world of the text belong to Situate, which runs alongside; Decompose only needs the words and the reading question.
how_it_works.the method does: reads the passage sentence by sentence, marks each small action as a move, labels who does it, the operation, what it acts on, and the result, and records how the moves connect (one feeds the next, one reports another's speech).
how_it_works.you get back: an ordered list of moves, and the connections between them.

on_mark_16.what_counts_as_one_move: One move is one agent doing one operation to one thing, with one result. Start a new move when the agent changes, the operation changes, or the result changes. When in doubt, keep the move whole rather than splitting it: an under-split reading loses less than an over-split one.

the_anatomy_of_a_move.note: A move is coded in two steps. FIRST classify its KIND (process_type: a doing, a sensing, a being, a saying, an existing) - the funnel decides how the parts read (a being or an existing has no agent). THEN fill the five core parts and the modifiers that hang under them. Each piece below carries its handle, its definition, its vocabulary, whether you pick one value or more than one, and whether you may propose a candidate when nothing fits. This is the grammar itself, text-agnostic; the worked example applies it to Mark 16.

funnel.definition: what KIND of move it is - a doing (material), a sensing (mental), a being (relational), a saying (verbal), or an existing (existential). Asked FIRST; it decides how the parts read (a being or an existing has no agent).

core.definition: who is telling the move: the teller whose voice presents it.
who or what performs the operation. Empty for a being or an existing; can be a person, a group, or the cosmos.
the act the move makes: the verb, what is done.
what the operation acts on (its case-roles are below).
what the move produces (may be empty).

modifiers.definition: how the claim is warranted: from experience, reason, testimony, revelation, or tradition.
is the narrator describing what IS or prescribing what OUGHT - it catches a prescription phrased as a plain statement.
the teller's attitude or reliability: sincere, ironic, aporetic, or unreliable.
the doer's kind: a person, a group, an impersonal or cosmic force, or none.
the verb's diathesis: does the agent perform the act (active), undergo it (passive), or both at once (middle).
the KIND of operation - an open label the coder writes (motion, transfer, perception...).
the proposition's relation to reality: it happened (realis), is obligated (deontic), is possible (epistemic), or is a capacity (dynamic).
affirmed, denied, or unsaid-on-purpose (apophatic = negation-as-method, 'not this, not this').
for a saying, the act the utterance performs: assert, command, question, promise, perform, express. Not-applicable otherwise.
the case-roles the operation takes: ON (the direct object), TO (the recipient), OF (the of-relation), WITH (the instrument), IN (the locus). More than one can apply at once.
what kind of thing the substrate is: an entity, a state, a reference to another move, and so on.
the outcome's status: achieved (actual), aimed-at (sought), or stated as future-certain (promised).

_render.note: Render the funnel (process_type) first; then the five core part-handles in the part colour (orange); then the modifiers grouped under their part in the modifier colour (green). For each closed field show its vocab + single-or-multi + candidate (the controlled-value contract); the substrate case-roles (on/to/of/with/in) are one multi-value slot. `leans_on` is the framework each field stands on (for the Foundation section).

worked_example.note: The grammar applied to Mark 16, move by move, so you can see the text become a sequence of small labeled actions. These are the first 12 of 60 moves; the full list is the feed the reading room renders. Across the passage the funnel sorts the moves by kind: material 28 · verbal 14 · mental 13 · existential 3 · relational 2.

moves.plain: The three named women acquire burial ointments once the rest-day ends.
moves.agent: Mary Magdalene, Mary the mother of James, and Salome
moves.outcome: spices in hand for an intended anointing of the corpse

moves.plain: At first light on the week's first day the same women arrive at the burial-cave.
moves.outcome: arrival at the tomb at sunrise

moves.plain: On the way they voice a worry to one another about who could shift the tomb's stone.
moves.outcome: a shared question laid on the table between them

moves.plain: The question itself: some unnamed helper is sought to displace the stone on their behalf.
moves.outcome: clearance of the entrance, hoped for

moves.plain: The narrator glosses in the reason for their worry: the sealing-stone is oversized.
moves.outcome: the stone stands as an obstacle

moves.plain: Raising their eyes, the women register visually that the barrier is already displaced.
moves.outcome: a perceived fact enters their awareness

moves.plain: The seen state itself: the sealing-stone has already been displaced by some unnamed force.
The women cross the threshold into the burial chamber.
moves.outcome: they are now inside the chamber

moves.plain: Inside, they perceive an unfamiliar figure seated in the chamber.
moves.outcome: an unexpected figure enters their awareness

moves.plain: The seen state: a young figure in white is present and seated on the chamber's right.
moves.substrate_in: the right side of the tomb
moves.outcome: an angelic-coded figure is stably present in the chamber

moves.plain: The women's inward response to the figure is stunned alarm.
moves.outcome: a state of fearful astonishment settles on them

moves.plain: The figure directs speech to them.
moves.outcome: a message is delivered to them

featured_moves.plain: The three named women acquire burial ointments once the rest-day ends.
featured_moves.agent: Mary Magdalene, Mary the mother of James, and Salome
featured_moves.outcome: spices in hand for an intended anointing of the corpse

featured_moves.plain: He names the object of their quest: the Nazarene who was executed by crucifixion.
featured_moves.substrate_on: Jesus of Nazareth, the crucified one

featured_moves.plain: He warrants the promise by pointing back to Jesus' own earlier prediction to the disciples.
featured_moves.outcome: the going-before-and-seeing is recognised as prior word now fulfilled

featured_moves.plain: The women bolt out of the burial chamber in flight.
featured_moves.outcome: they are away from the tomb, in flight

connections.plain: The 49 connections are of two kinds: 37 nesting (one move scopes over others, for example the young man's speech contains the announcement 'he has been raised') and 12 reporting (one move reports another's speech). Not every move links to another, so there are fewer connections than moves.

on_mark_16.the_silence_thread: Watch the pair M22 (the women flee the tomb) and M23 (they say nothing to anyone). The women are told to carry the resurrection news, and instead they say nothing. That silence is the ending the whole reading turns on. Follow this pair through every later step.

where_saved.plain: The moves save to the corpus, in the source_move table (one row per move), with their connections in source_move_edge. They join back to this passage through the same home the checkout opened: this passage's row in the text_checkout table (its id is gut-8268_016_v1), which you find by the method key MARK-16-WEB. So the moves, and every step built on them, sit in one findable place with the text they came from.

honest_limits: These moves were read from a retyped copy of the text, not yet from the library checkout, so the wording is a paraphrase. Re-run this step on the verbatim checkout text (a clean run on the real words rather than the retyped copy) and the moves refresh from the real words.
This is one coder on one pass, a reference reading, not a reliability-tested one yet.

how_to_run.step 1, get the passage: Start from the checkout (the Text step, which hands over the exact sourced passage). Today the extractor reads a text file; a clean run on the verbatim checkout text feeds it the real words rather than the retyped copy.
how_to_run.step 2, extract the moves: ./scripts/_run_python.sh scripts/analysis/engine1_layer1_extract_moves.py --text <passage file> --source-key MARK-16-WEB --qud "What is the resurrection, and who transmits it?" --sitz-year 70
how_to_run.what each input means: --text is the passage to read. --source-key is the method key for this text (MARK-16-WEB), the same key that joins to the checkout home. --qud is the fixed Question Under Discussion (load-bearing: it decides what counts as salient). --sitz-year is the composition year.
how_to_run.step 4, where it saves: source_move (the moves) and source_move_edge (the connections), keyed on the method key, joined to the text_checkout home.
how_to_run.then: Situate runs in parallel; then the gaps.
